principle: NN/g #3 User control & freedom (clearly-marked exit); WCAG 2.2 §2.4.7 Focus not obscured; Apple HIG modal sheet pattern; Fitts's Law
location: /projects → PLANNER → COVERAGE spectrum grid → gap-fill popover [role=dialog].frame-strong (button[role=gridcell] trigger)
problem: Tapping an UPPER-viewport spectrum cell at 375x667 opens the gap-fill popover as a fixed ANCHORED popover, NOT a bottom sheet. Measured computed style: position:fixed, top:-305.3px, bottom:60px (stretched between a broken top and the bottom anchor). Resulting header top=-205px and the '× Close gap-fill popover' button top=-197px — both fully OFF-SCREEN above the viewport. Dialog overflowY:hidden and not scrollable, so the close cannot be revealed. Escape key does NOT dismiss. Only a tap on another cell dismisses it (accidental). The max-md: bottom-sheet utilities ARE in the class list (max-md:!top-auto max-md:inset-x-2 max-md:bottom-[calc(60px+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]) and the (max-width:767px) media query matches, but max-md:!top-auto is NOT winning — computed top resolved to -305px instead of auto. This is viewport-HEIGHT dependent: on 414x896 the same broken CSS leaves the close at top=68px (on-screen, incidental pass), but on the stated primary 375x667 the header is unreachable. The Round-15 fix did not actually convert this to a bottom sheet.
fix: The `max-md:!top-auto` Tailwind utility is not being emitted/applied in the production CSS (the !important + top-auto under a stacked max-md variant compiles to nothing while `bottom` arbitrary value applies). Stop relying on a JIT'd `!top-auto`. Either (a) add an explicit rule in globals.css: `@media (max-width:767px){ [data-gapfill-popover]{ top:auto !important; bottom:calc(60px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom,0px)) !important; left:0 !important; right:0 !important; inset-inline:0 !important; max-height:70vh; border-radius:12px 12px 0 0; } }` and tag the dialog with data-gapfill-popover; or (b) render two distinct trees: a true bottom-sheet component under md and the anchored popover at md+. Verify on 375x667 that the [role=dialog] computes top:auto / bottom anchored and the × close button getBoundingClientRect().top >= 0. Also add Escape-to-dismiss and a tap-scrim backdrop.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow (no horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px); Refactoring UI — content must fit the column
location: /library LIST view (and default view) — .caret-row rows + footer '7,144 paints' bar + owned/★ control cluster (.flex.items-center.gap-1.shrink-0.ml-auto)
problem: /library LIST view still overflows horizontally. At 375: documentElement.scrollWidth=431 vs clientWidth=360 (71px overflow). At 768: scrollWidth=949 vs clientWidth=753 (196px overflow). The ticket required scrollWidth==clientWidth. The owned/★ columns are NOT both visible: the 'Mark as owned' (○) button is at L312–R356 (visible) but the 'Mark as wanted' (★) button sits at L360–R404 — OFF-SCREEN past the right edge. The default (grid) view shows the same overflow (.caret-row width=416px inside a 360 container despite w-full max-w-full overflow-hidden). The 'VIEW ... LIST' header label is itself clipped at the right edge.
fix: The .caret-row content cluster with `ml-auto` is pushing the owned/★ buttons beyond the row's clip box; overflow-hidden hides paint but the row's own intrinsic width (416/431px) still drives documentElement.scrollWidth. Constrain the row to the viewport: set the scroll container and each .caret-row to `width:100%; max-width:100%; box-sizing:border-box` AND ensure the name/brand text block is `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate` so it yields space; the owned/★ cluster must be `flex-none` (not pushed by ml-auto past the edge). Drop ml-auto on mobile (max-md:ml-0) and use justify-between on the row. The footer '7,144 paints' bar (px-3, w=431) needs `w-full max-w-full box-border`. Re-verify scrollWidth==clientWidth at 375 AND 768 and that both ○ and ★ toggles have right <= clientWidth.

principle: Touch target separation / Fitts's Law; WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size; NN/g #5 Error prevention
location: /recipes/[id] → STEPS · SLOT row → swatch button (aria 'Change paint for step') overlapping × (aria 'Delete step')
problem: The technique <select> half of the fix landed (it shrank to 120px, no longer collides). BUT the step swatch and the × delete still OVERLAP. Measured at 375: swatch 'Change paint for step' = L249–R293 (44x44); 'Delete step' × = L271–R315 (44x44). They overlap by 22px (271→293), and the × is partially clipped at the screen edge (R315 > usable area). A recruit aiming for the swatch can hit Delete and vice-versa. select_x_delete_overlap=false (good), but swatch_x_delete_overlap=true (bad).
fix: In the step row flex container, give the swatch and the ×-delete each `flex-none` and a real gap between them (gap-2 / 8px min) so their 44px boxes don't overlap, and ensure the row doesn't exceed the viewport (the × right edge 315 is near the 360 edge — fine once gap is added, but verify R(delete) <= clientWidth). Confirm swatch_x_delete_overlap=false after the change. The select already shrinks correctly below lg; do not touch it.

verdict: PARTIAL (logic shipped, build-stamp broken; net behavior OK)
principle: Doherty Threshold / Visibility of system status — returning users must get the current build; cache-busting correctness
problem: The UX-1505 versioning LOGIC shipped correctly: sw.js has skipWaiting (true), clients.claim (true), derives SHELL_CACHE=`mm-shell-${BUILD_ID}` / DATA_CACHE=`mm-data-${BUILD_ID}`, KEEP_CACHES, and an activate handler that deletes every cache not in KEEP_CACHES. HOWEVER the build-time stamp did NOT run: the literal token '__BUILD_ID__' was never replaced, so `.startsWith('__')` is true and BUILD_ID falls back to the constant string 'dev'. Live cache name is therefore 'mm-shell-dev' on EVERY deploy — the exact 'fixed literal that never changes across deploys' failure UX-1505 set out to eliminate. Per-build cache versioning is non-functional. MITIGATION (why net behavior is acceptable): the cache only stores static shell assets (manifest.json + 4 icons) — NOT HTML and NOT JS bundles. Navigations are network-first (HTML not cached); JS is fetched fresh from /_next. So returning-user reloads DO serve the fresh build. Tested: cleared SW+caches, cold load fired one React #418 on first paint (see UX-1508); a second load (returning-user reload) served clean with ZERO console errors and no #418. Old caches are cleaned by the activate handler. So stale-build risk is low in practice, but the versioning mechanism the ticket claims is not actually operating.
fix: Wire the build-time replacement so __BUILD_ID__ is substituted with a per-deploy value (e.g. process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA or NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_ID) by the sw stamp script during `next build` / postbuild. Verify in prod that caches.keys() returns mm-shell-<sha> (NOT mm-shell-dev) and that the name changes between two deploys. The runtime logic itself is correct and needs no change.

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status; React hydration correctness (Minified React error #418 — server/client HTML mismatch)
location: First cold paint after SW+cache clear — /projects (chunk 0t2ge5s_3fi8z.js). Hydration mismatch (#418 args[]=HTML).
problem: On the FIRST cold load (fresh context, SW + caches cleared at session start — i.e. NOT a stale-shell scenario), React Minified error #418 fired: 'Text content does not match server-rendered HTML / hydration mismatch (args[]=HTML)'. Because caches were cleared, this is NOT caused by an old SW shell — it is a genuine SSR/CSR hydration mismatch in the app (likely date/locale, streak count '1 day', or Date('today, June 2 2026') rendered server-side vs client-side, or an Online/ON indicator differing on first paint). On the SECOND load (returning-user reload) it did not reproduce — so it is timing/first-paint sensitive, not persistent. UX-1505 claimed to remove the #418; it still fires on cold load.
fix: Find the component rendering different markup on server vs client at first paint. Most likely candidates given the snapshot: the calendar 'Today, June 2 2026' cell (Date computed at render time), the STREAK '1 day' count, or the header 'Online/ON' navigator.onLine read. Gate any client-only / time-dependent value behind a mounted flag (useEffect setMounted) or suppressHydrationWarning on the specific node, or compute the date deterministically on the server and pass it as a prop. Re-test: hard cold load at 375 must show 0 console errors.
